tagline: A loop from a Bavarian Helen up around the Chattahoochee's source.
intro: The loop starts outside Helen, a logging town in decline that remade itself as a Bavarian alpine village. Zoning since 1969 has required the look on every building, the few national franchises included. From there SR 17/75 runs north into the Chattahoochee National Forest, and the road circles the headwaters of the Chattahoochee River through valleys and mountain gaps.
SR 180 runs west past the spur up Brasstown Bald, and SR 348 brings the loop back southeast. It is about 40 miles. The Forest Service says to allow at least three hours.
season: The Forest Service calls the drive ideal for wildflowers or fall color.

moments.title: Brasstown Bald
moments.text: Georgia's highest point owes its English name to settlers who mistook the Cherokee for "New Green Place" for the word for brass. On a clear day Atlanta's towers show 85 miles off.

moments.title: Hogpen Gap
moments.text: Here the byway crosses the Appalachian Trail.

moments.title: Dukes Creek Falls
moments.text: Gold turned up on Dukes Creek in 1828 and set off the Georgia Gold Rush. A 2.2-mile round trip now leads to a pool below the 150-foot falls.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Russell-Brasstown National Scenic Byway
